title: I built a stealth game where your only light can give you away — now with 4 levels
author: Training-Machine-943
selftext:
**Srirangam, 14th century. A sacred deity must disappear before the invaders find it.**

I’ve been experimenting with **Spawn.co’s AI game-making tools** to turn a story from my upcoming book, *The Self-Driving Mind*, into a playable historical adventure.

In **Srirangam: God in Exile**, you play a temple priest carrying Sri Namperumal to safety. Protect the flame, avoid the guards, escape Srirangam, and journey through the wilderness to Tirumala.  
  
Your oil lamp is both your lifeline and your biggest risk. Walking consumes oil. An open flame attracts patrols. Cupping it helps you hide—but slows you down. Shrines offer checkpoints along the way.

[A sacred deity must disappear before the invaders find it.](https://preview.redd.it/2gjtgeg0o4rh1.png?width=748&format=png&auto=webp&s=dc3c86dd66923172f5dfff00b433bfeae0ee9999)

I started this as an experiment—I didn’t know Savi from Savvy until this weekend—but Savi/Spawn has let me take it much further than I expected. It now has **four playable levels**, including the new **Tirumala level**. The clip shows the journey in order, from the courtyard to the final sanctuary.

It’s **free to play on desktop and mobile**, with a ***watchable demo*** and ***guided practice***. On mobile, play in landscape.

[**Play Srirangam: God in Exile**](https://www.spawn.co/@self_driving_mind/srirangam-god-in-exile/play)

The game draws on a historical story I wrote on Substack, also linked inside the game: [**They Stole the God First, Then Came…**](https://selfdrivingmind.substack.com/p/they-stole-the-god-first-then-came?r=6gle0t)

**What would you improve next—gameplay, difficulty, atmosphere, or storytelling?**
